linkedin.title: Personalised news is currently broken.
linkedin.body:
Most algorithms today are designed to keep you scrolling, not to keep you informed. They feed you more of what you already like, creating a feedback loop that narrows your world instead of expanding it. That is the opposite of what news should do.

We are building Headlinne to change that. The next phase of personalised news is not about showing you more of the same. It is about giving you context. It is about understanding that you might care about a local infrastructure project, a global tech trend, and a niche hobby at the same time.

True personalisation should be about utility. It should filter out the noise so you can spend less time searching for quality information and more time actually understanding it. We are focusing on tools that help you digest complex topics quickly, without stripping away the nuance that matters.

Technology should work for the reader, not the platform. We are moving away from engagement metrics and toward genuine clarity.

story_card.headline: Why human brains take years to develop
story_card.standfirst: Scientists found immune cells in our brains mature much slower than previously thought.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Researchers found that human brain immune cells take up to eight years to fully mature.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: In mice, these same cells called microglia finish developing in only a few weeks.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: This slow growth helps shape brain circuits and likely drives our unique cognitive abilities.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Further research into this human-only gene process and its role in brain complexity.

story_card.caption:
Scientists have discovered why human brain development is so different from other mammals.

Immune cells in our brains, known as microglia, take four to eight years to reach maturity. This prolonged timeline is key to building the complex circuits that give humans our advanced cognitive skills.
